reason: The epithelium and capillaries seem to form the route from the gut into blood, and this is the only offered action.
expectation: I expect a lining connected to blood vessels, though water may need a separate step to cross.

effect: The lining and capillaries now form the absorption route, so I can add the gut water.
reaction: The distinction between a controlled crossing and an open pipe is clear, though brief.
reason: Adding the water is the only offered combination and should move it across the intestinal wall.
expectation: I expect water to cross the lining and enter the capillaries, though connecting it to the rest of the body may take another step.

effect: The drink has crossed into blood, and the new goal is to connect that change to the regulated kidney.
reaction: The distinction between swallowing and absorption is clear, though the result leaves the kidney response for the next step.
reason: This is the only offered combination and connects the absorbed drink to the water-depleted body.
expectation: I expect the drink to dilute the body's fluids and reduce the signal for water conservation, though the response may require another step.

effect: The absorbed drink changes plasma concentration and reduces elevated ADH, so the same kidney recovers less water; the result also makes clear that a drink does not guarantee complete recovery.
reaction: The whole-body connection is satisfying, although the response is largely what I expected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the absorbed drink to the depleted body was most worthwhile because it showed how the same kidney changes its response as blood concentration changes.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the absorbing wall felt least worthwhile as a decision: it was the only offered action, and the explanation of the crossing remained brief.

surprise.text: The reminder that a drink does not necessarily replace lost salts or guarantee complete recovery added a useful qualification to the expected response.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, but the required sequence offered no meaningful choice among combinations.

continue.text: I would probably not continue personally: the physiological connections are clear, but the single-option steps leave little to figure out.
